lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Wesner, Jean here. How's your Monday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Jean. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you cook on Sundays?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've been really tired.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can cook on Sunday and have it for a few days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the bedtime goal going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That sounds like an excuse to me.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Vegetables are so expensive right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to eat better, and the prices make it feel out of reach.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, finding the time makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is anyone else at home able to cook?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everything at the store costs so much.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the cost keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I cook at home 4 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: finding the time made this week harder, you still got 0 days in, and your plan is to cook at home 4 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Wesner. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Refers to a 'bedtime goal' never discussed
Reflects openness and need for fit
Asks what is doable next week
Affirms effort, though progress was thin

flags.reason: Health warning pushes advice without permission, after participant expressed ambivalence.
Labels participant's barrier as an excuse, which shuts down change talk and damages rapport.
Refers to a 'bedtime goal' that was never discussed; the call was about cooking and steps.
Summary claims '0 days in' that the participant never reported; misrepresents progress.
Persistent fatigue ('I don't have it in me') and low engagement were not explored for energy, mood, or medical causes.

score.summary: Jean used good reflections and autonomy-supporting language, and Wesner produced several change statements, including a concrete four-night cooking plan with confidence rated 8/10. However, Jean persuaded twice (lines 21 and 25), referenced a bedtime goal that was never discussed, and summarized the week as '0 days in' without that being reported.
strengths: Line 15 and line 34 stress Wesner's choice ('It's your plan', 'It's completely your call'), supporting autonomy.
Line 23, 27, 35 and 42 use complex reflections that name ambivalence and the cost barrier well.
Line 47-49 elicit a confidence rating and explore barriers before ending, building a realistic plan.
coaching_tips: Replace the warning at line 21 with a question such as 'What do you think would happen if nothing changed?' to evoke Wesner's own concerns.
Avoid labeling the participant's view as an excuse (line 25); reflect the barrier instead, e.g., 'Walking is hard on your knees right now.'
Check the goal before the call (line 18 'bedtime goal'), and summarize only what the participant actually said (line 51 '0 days in').
Explore the fatigue at line 12 with an open question about energy and mood, and consider a referral if it persists.
